title: Multi-Stage Pipeline Design
description: Structure one YAML pipeline that builds once and promotes the same artifact through dev, staging, and production.

data.text: Three separate pipelines build the same code for dev, staging, and production. The production build sometimes differs from what was tested in staging because it was compiled minutes later from a different commit. Design a pipeline where what you test is exactly what you ship.

Use a **single multi-stage YAML pipeline** that builds the artifact **once** and publishes it, then deploys that immutable artifact to each stage. Configuration differences belong in **variable groups** or app settings, never in a rebuild. Attach **Environments** with approval checks to staging and production so promotion is a deliberate, auditable act.

data.title: azure-pipelines.yml — build once, deploy many
data.code:
trigger:
  branches: { include: [ main ] }

variables:
  - group: quotient-shared
  - name: buildConfiguration
    value: Release

stages:
  - stage: Build
    jobs:
      - job: BuildAndTest
        pool: { vmImage: ubuntu-latest }
        steps:
          - task: UseDotNet@2
            inputs: { version: '8.x' }
          - script: dotnet test --configuration $(buildConfiguration)
            displayName: Run tests
          - script: dotnet publish -c $(buildConfiguration) -o $(Build.ArtifactStagingDirectory)/app
            displayName: Publish
          - publish: $(Build.ArtifactStagingDirectory)/app
            artifact: drop

  - stage: Dev
    dependsOn: Build
    variables:
      - group: quotient-dev
    jobs:
      - deployment: DeployDev
        environment: dev
        strategy:
          runOnce:
            deploy:
              steps:
                - download: current
                  artifact: drop
                - task: AzureWebApp@1
                  inputs:
                    azureSubscription: quotient-dev-connection
                    appName: $(appName)
                    package: $(Pipeline.Workspace)/drop

  - stage: Production
    dependsOn: [ Build, Dev ]
    condition: succeeded()
    variables:
      - group: quotient-prod
    jobs:
      - deployment: DeployProd
        environment: production   # approval check configured on this environment
        strategy:
          runOnce:
            deploy:
              steps:
                - download: current
                  artifact: drop
                - task: AzureWebApp@1
                  inputs:
                    azureSubscription: quotient-prod-connection
                    appName: $(appName)
                    package: $(Pipeline.Workspace)/drop

data.text: Rebuilding per environment reintroduces risk: dependency versions drift between builds, and the artifact tested is not the artifact shipped. A single build with promoted artifacts also makes rollback trivial — redeploy the previous immutable artifact instead of rebuilding old source.

cards.title: Single multi-stage pipeline
cards.description: Build once, promote the same artifact
pros: One place to read the deployment path
Simple rollback to a prior artifact

cards.title: Separate pipeline per environment
cards.description: Independent build and release per stage
pros: Teams can own a stage end to end
